findings.title: Point ① can pass on a design approval whose reviewed plan blob was never verified, and the plan promotes that pass to merge authority
findings.detail: The writer gate in §4.1(2) is defined only as 'alignment/conflict/coverage all pass and overall can'. In packages/teamlead/src/ship-judgment/evidence-ledger.ts:308-330, when EvidenceAuthorityReader.designApproval() returns no expectedBlobSha (evidence-authority.ts:70-84 only attaches it when a design_review_manifest row matches execution_id AND expected_plan_path AND is_current=1), the design_review evidence ref is merely LABELLED 'blob_unverified' and plan_at_head is satisfied by the mere existence of non-empty text at the reviewed path at head (production-collect.ts:224-242 reads the blob from HEAD with no comparison to what was reviewed). The repo's own test asserts this exact state: ship-judgment/__tests__/evidence-ledger.test.ts:92-104 has a fixture with designApproval lacking expectedBlobSha and asserts alignment.verdict === 'pass' together with label 'blob_unverified'. The model cannot rescue this because applySemanticEvidence (evidence-ledger.ts:427-454) is veto-only: it can turn pass into fail, never the reverse, and an 'undetermined' semantic result does not veto. Under FLY-2399's dry_run scope 'blob_unverified' was an honest display caveat; this plan turns the same verdict into a durable approve + land. The plan never uses the words blob/expectedBlobSha/plan_at_head anywhere, so an implementer following it literally ships the hole. The plan must state that the auto writer additionally requires a blob-verified design approval (expectedBlobSha present AND matching the plan blob at the approved head) and must add an acceptance row for it.
findings.failure_scenario: Issue FLY-X has an APPROVED codex design review on engineering/doc/FLY-X/plan.md whose design_review_manifest row is absent or whose expected_plan_path does not byte-match codex_review_job.target_path, so designApproval.expectedBlobSha is undefined. The runner then rewrites plan.md at the PR head to describe whatever the diff actually does. buildEvidenceLedger labels the design ref 'blob_unverified' but still returns alignment.verdict='pass'; code review at head is APPROVED, mechanical is pass, QA claim is qa_passed, so overall='can'. commitShipJudgmentSourceIfEligible sees 'all three pass and overall can', writes the approve source, the projector mints the founder_verdict/claim, and land-executor merges a PR whose stated design authority is a document the reviewer never saw.

findings.title: Point ③ ('QA report covers all use cases') can pass with zero QA report bytes ever read, yet the plan treats that pass as sufficient to auto-approve
findings.detail: In evidence-ledger.ts:355-366, coverage is decided entirely by qaAuthority (a workflow_claims qa_verdict row with predicate 'qa_passed'); the hosted QA report contributes only an optional evidence ref — 'if (m?.qaReport) ref(c, "qa_report", ...)' — and its ABSENCE never produces missing() or fail(). readClaimQaSource (qa-source.ts:13-46) returns null on many non-verdict grounds (summary carries no selectable report reference, URL not classified as hosted_report, body empty or >262144 bytes, registry read throws), and production-collect.ts:246-255 then simply leaves material.qaReport unset while qaAuthority stays 'pass'. The model cannot compensate: evaluate.ts:127-131 forces the model's coverage verdict to 'undetermined' whenever the packet carries no 'qa' source, and applySemanticEvidence only vetoes on 'fail', so an 'undetermined' coverage passes through while resultCode stays 'evaluated' — i.e. §4.1(2)'s 'durable successful evaluation' requirement is satisfied and still nothing blocks. The repo fixture proves it: evidence-ledger.test.ts:62-71 sets qaAuthority pass with no qaReport key and line 92-98 asserts coverage.verdict === 'pass'. The founder's own criterion ③ is about the REPORT, and the plan's own acceptance row C (line 151) promises 'missing QA/use case ... no approve', but §4.1 never states the design change needed to make that true. The plan must require, for the auto writer only, that coverage evidence include an actually-read QA report bound to the approved head (and that a semantic coverage result of 'undetermined' is a deny, not a non-veto).
findings.failure_scenario: A qa node issues a permanent qa_verdict claim with predicate 'qa_passed' at the exact head, but its summary contains no hosted-report URL (or the report host registry read fails), so readClaimQaSource returns null. buildEvidenceLedger gives coverage.verdict='pass' with only a qa_claim ref and no qa_report ref; the evaluator, handed a packet with no 'qa' source, legally returns coverage='undetermined' with resultCode='evaluated'; applySemanticEvidence sets coverageVeto=false. overall='can', the card renders '③ QA 用例覆盖：通过', the writer commits an approve source and the PR lands although no QA report was ever fetched or judged.

findings.title: Plan keeps the existing 120-request/hour project refresh budget unchanged although that budget is already known to starve the three-point chain at real PR inventory
findings.detail: §3 says 'Keep current model/source budgets' and §4.1(3) additionally requires a freshly re-collected, 0-60s-old mechanical validation on every auto attempt. project-refresh.ts:423-443 enforces a project-wide rolling budget of 120 GitHub API reservations per hour, and ProjectCache.read() (project-refresh.ts:568-580) hard-expires the snapshot at 60s, so every approval attempt whose snapshot has aged out needs a full refresh. A prior QA pass on this same chain (FLY-2560) recorded that a refresh at ~42 in-flight PRs needs ~136 requests, i.e. it cannot complete inside the 120/h budget at all, which makes both the mechanical snapshot and the PR diff permanently unavailable. That fails closed (mechanical -> undetermined -> overall undetermined -> no approve), so it is not ship-unsafe, but it means the feature this plan designs may be unable to approve anything in production, and the plan carries no risk note, no dependency on a budget/pagination fix, and no acceptance row for it. Add it explicitly as a stated precondition or a known limitation.
findings.failure_scenario: Flywheel has ~40+ open PRs. The scanner's shared refresh exhausts the 120/h reservation before finishing, throws ProjectFetchFailure('request_budget_or_lease'), and ProjectCache.read() returns undefined for the rest of the hour. Every auto attempt falls into unknown('input_unavailable:...'), conflict stays undetermined, overall stays undetermined, and no card is ever auto-approved — the shipped feature is inert while the plan and founder page describe it as live.

findings.title: §2's render disposition only names the legacy-summary lines, leaving the hardcoded '仍由你批准' / '· dry_run' copy unaddressed on a card that will self-approve
findings.detail: render.ts hardcodes '**机器试判：...** · dry_run' (line 52 and line 74) and '截至 ${view.mechanical.checkedAt} 的试判；后续检查可能待更新，仍由你批准。' (lines 59 and 94) in BOTH render branches. §2's disposition for render.ts only says 'remove legacy summary API and render lines', which reads as the '旧窄口三闸/样本统计' line; §3 introduces a new action line and '三点机器判断' language but never names these two strings. An implementer executing §2 literally leaves an auto-mode card that asserts '仍由你批准' immediately before the writer approves it — exactly the class of false founder-facing statement this issue exists to remove. Separately, checkedAt is deliberately excluded from presentationDigest (opinions.ts:161-177) so a revalidated pass-to-pass refresh legitimately does NOT repost; the posted text therefore keeps showing an older '截至 <time>' than the freshness the writer actually validated against. §3's claim 'presentation content is identical' is not literally true for that line. Name both strings in the plan and say which timestamp (if any) the auto card should display.
findings.failure_scenario: Mode is auto, the card is delivered and validated, evidence is refreshed pass-to-pass so no PATCH is issued, and the writer approves. The founder sees a card reading '机器试判：可 · dry_run ... 截至 2026-09-18T10:00:00Z 的试判；后续检查可能待更新，仍由你批准。' while the PR has already been machine-approved on evidence validated at 10:41Z.

findings.title: Retaining the `auto_merge_narrow_gate` identifier after the policy stops being narrow leaves config/CLI output actively misleading
findings.detail: §3 keeps the stored key `auto_merge_narrow_gate` for compatibility and only changes the human label to '三点自动审批'. The key is what appears in flag dumps, StateStore rows, `getFlagValueRow('auto_merge_narrow_gate','flywheel')` call sites and any operator grep; after this change `auto_merge_narrow_gate=auto` no longer means 'narrow pure-docs auto-merge' but 'any change that clears three points is auto-approved'. §7 task 5 updates the protected flag description, which helps, but the plan should also require a one-line deprecation comment at every remaining read site (StateStore.ts:59616, flag-store-runtime.ts:163) so the next reader is not misled by the name alone.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator triaging an incident greps the flag store, sees `auto_merge_narrow_gate: auto`, recalls FLY-2399's docs-only scope, and concludes no code PR could have been machine-approved — while the widened policy is exactly what approved it.

findings.title: §7 states the listed test filenames are new additions, but `approval-writer.integration.test.ts` already exists
findings.detail: The suggested command block lists `src/ship-judgment/__tests__/approval-writer.integration.test.ts` and the following sentence says 'New test filenames in commands are proposed additions'. That file already exists and covers the FOUNDER ship-approval writer (it imports founder-ship-approval-factory, founder-approval-projector and founder-reply-deliverer). Appending the machine-writer cases there mixes two distinct authority paths in one suite and makes the plan's own 'preserve test counts' discipline harder to audit. Name a distinct file (e.g. `ship-judgment-auto-approval.integration.test.ts`) or state explicitly that the existing suite is being extended and what its current count is. The same paragraph's hedge 'where present' already covers `clarifications.test.ts`, which likewise does not exist.
findings.failure_scenario: Implement adds machine-writer cases into the existing founder-writer suite; a later reviewer comparing 'expected test count' against the plan cannot tell which assertions are new, and a regression that silently deletes founder-path cases while adding machine-path cases nets out to an unchanged count.
